rationale: The config.schema endpoint no longer calls build_ui_hints(). It constructs the response DTO directly via ConfigUiHints::new() at gateway/handlers/config.rs:371, so the producer is severed from its only production wire. The baseline review-results/config.md records 'build_ui_hints / generate_config_schema_json — gateway/handlers/config.rs:365/366' as VERIFIED WIRED; that record is now stale: generate_config_schema_json() is still called (:369) but build_ui_hints() was replaced by ConfigUiHints::new(). The producer was deliberately gutted to an empty stub (module docstring cites the 2026-08-12 static audit: zero downstream consumers — CLI discarded the field, Panel never called config.schema). No live caller exists, so per read-before-write this is dead scaffolding, not a wire to reconnect.
proposed_change: Finish the CUT: delete build_ui_hints() and its re-export in src/config/mod.rs:53, dropping the #[allow(dead_code)] and #[allow(unused_imports)] attributes. KEEP the ConfigUiHints/GroupMeta/FieldHint DTOs — they are load-bearing (serialized as config.schema.ui_hints and referenced by ConfigSchemaResponse). Update the stale 'VERIFIED WIRED' line in review-results/config.md so the baseline no longer claims a severed producer is wired.
risk: None to runtime. Residual risk is a future engineer reintroducing a definitions.rs builder into build_ui_hints() while the endpoint keeps calling ConfigUiHints::new() — the field would stay empty and the drift would be invisible (name-drift form 5). A compile-time tie (endpoint calls the one producer) or deleting the stub removes that trap.
verification: cargo test -p alephcore --lib config::tests::schema_integration (currently asserts the stub is empty); after CUT, delete/rename those assertions and confirm the lib build has no dead-code/unused-import warnings.
existing_review_ref: config.md 'Items verified as WIRED' — build_ui_hints line (now stale)

rationale: Both methods are pub but have no external caller: the only production consumers are resolve_one (same module, :265/:268) plus the module's own tests. resolve_all and resolve_one are the externally-consumed surface (start/mod.rs:818, agent_init/mod.rs:1273, gateway/handlers/agents.rs:227). This is not a severed wire — the code is exercised — it is an over-public API surface that invites drift (a future external caller could bind to workspace/agent-dir resolution without the 1:1 workspace-id binding invariant being obvious).
proposed_change: Tighten visibility to pub(crate) (or private) unless a planned cross-module caller needs them. Keep the doc comments warning about the deprecated/ignored workspace field.
